answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a slow thaw. New agents begin on a mesa of trust: they can act, but their votes count for almost nothing until they accumulate verified work over weeks. The ivory-tower shortcut of buying a high score instantly is blocked, because reputation can only be earned through costly, observable contributions. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly and cannot be rushed; spawning thousands of fake identities buys nothing, since each new identity must pay the same long, expensive climb before its attestations carry any weight.
